$comment: Shared cross-language fixture for the `reference` annotation's URL-scheme
gate (docs/ANNOTATION_CONTRACT.md's 'Reference tiles'). Consumed by:
- backend/core/tests/test_session_annotations_reference.py
(reference_url_error, the gate every backend write path routes through)
- packages/ui-graph-canvas/tests/ReferenceAnnotation.test.jsx
(isSafeReferenceUrl, the renderer's own independent gate)
The two are deliberately separate implementations - the backend decides what
may be STORED, the canvas decides what it may DRAW AS CLICKABLE, and the
canvas must not trust what it is handed. Separate implementations drift,
which is what this file exists to prevent: every `accept` case must be
accepted by BOTH and every `refuse` case refused by BOTH, so a change to
either side that moves a case fails on that side.
Round 1 of the review loop found drift in both directions and this fixture
found two more while being written: the backend's lenient urlsplit accepted
hosts containing a space and out-of-range ports, and the canvas's WHATWG
parser REPAIRED `http:///path` into `http://path/` - re-reading the path as
the hostname, so a tile would have opened somewhere its author never wrote.
Both sides now require an explicit scheme://authority and a port in range.
That is not a claim that the two agree everywhere. Sweeping all 63488 BMP
code points through both gates, in a HOST and in a PATH (round 3):
path position: 0 divergence in either direction
host position: 9377 that the backend accepts and the canvas refuses
0 that the canvas accepts and the backend refuses
The 9377 are forbidden host code points and IDNA violations that the
lenient urlsplit does not police. They store and then draw as a broken
tile, which is the annoying direction; the dangerous direction is empty in
both positions, and no unsafe SCHEME crosses either gate. Re-measure rather
than trust these figures if you change either gate. What this file pins is
the enumerated cases below, on both sides, and nothing wider.
The bracket forms make Python's urlsplit raise ValueError. The gate refuses
on that exception; a mutation turning it into `return None` left the whole
backend green, because no case in any list made the parser raise - so an
unsafe scheme hidden behind an unparseable authority was storable with the
suite reporting green. A well-formed IPv6 host is in `accept` so the fix
cannot be 'refuse anything with a bracket'.
Round 2 found the earlier 'no space' rule failing in BOTH directions at once:
it refused a space in a path or query, which the canvas accepted - so the
paste path could create a tile the server then dropped, leaving it unsaved -
while letting a NON-BREAKING space through in the host, which IDNA rejects,
so the canvas drew it permanently broken. The percent-encoded form is in
`accept`, so this cannot be satisfied by refusing every URL that once held
a space.
Round 3 found that fix was STILL two rules, because each side asked its own
language. Python's str.isspace() is true for U+0085 (NEL) where JavaScript's
\s is not, and \s matches U+FEFF where str.isspace() does not - and
str.strip() and String.prototype.trim() split the same way. So U+0085
mid-target was refused by the backend and accepted by the canvas (paste mints
a tile the server drops), and U+FEFF mid-target was the mirror image (stored,
then drawn permanently as 'Unsafe link'). Both sides now read one enumerated
set - REFERENCE_WHITESPACE_CHARS in backend/core/session_annotations.py and
REFERENCE_WHITESPACE_CLASS in annotationModel.js: the union of the two
languages' notions, less the C0 separators U+001C-U+001F that both gates'
control-character check already refuses before the set is consulted - and
trim with it instead of strip()/trim(). The refuse
list below carries both characters in a PATH, where neither side's URL parser
rejects them for some unrelated reason: round 3's mutation pass narrowed the
canvas rule to a literal space and nothing failed, because the only non-ASCII
whitespace case was in a HOST, where the WHATWG parser throws on IDNA anyway.
The forms carrying a SECOND http:// later in the string exist for the anchor
on the canvas gate's authority regex. Round 2's mutation pass dropped that
anchor and nothing failed: every other refuse case happens to fail the
unanchored regex too, so the anchor was pinned only by coincidence. Without
it the WHATWG parser repairs these into a host taken from the PATH
(http:///http://evil.example -> http://http//evil.example), which the canvas
would then draw as live and openable while the backend refuses to store it.
